culture-cycles.note: Bank holidays notified for the RBI New Delhi office for 2026; state government offices usually close on these days too, but the state's own gazette list can differ. Where RBI shows several festival names for one day, the label lists all of them; the one that applies here is the festival observed in this state. Dates before 5 November 2026 have passed; replace with the 2027 list when RBI publishes it. Lunar and Islamic dates move each year.

laws.rule: Under the Delhi Excise Rules 2010 (rule 20), the quantities of liquor an individual may buy and possess are limited, and the rule applies to a person aged 25 or over: up to 9 litres of Indian or foreign spirits (whisky, rum, gin, vodka, brandy) and up to 18 litres of wine, beer, liqueur, cider and alcopop (a ready-mixed sweet alcoholic drink). A person bringing liquor into Delhi from another Indian state may carry 1 litre; from another country, 2 litres.
laws.heading: Delhi Excise Rules 2010, rule 20

laws.rule: Licensed clubs must not sell liquor to anyone under 25, even a member (rule 16, Delhi Excise Rules 2010). The Excise Department publishes dry-day orders (days when liquor sales are closed) on its website; they are issued as dated notices, for example 24 September 2026 and 26 May 2026, so check the current list.

local-law.note: Delhi is a union territory with its own excise law. Read from the department's copy of the 2010 Rules; amendments after that copy was posted were not checked.
